text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page. It’s the fastest way to let keyboard users bypass repetitive blocks like headers and nav bars, cutting navigation time from seconds to a single keystroke. The trade-off is one extra link in the DOM, but it’s invisible to mouse users and adds negligible weight.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is a persistent skip link in the top-left corner clutters the viewport for sighted keyboard users—it’s always visible, even when unnecessary. A better alternative is a skip link that only appears after the first tab press, then hides until the next page load, balancing discoverability and clutter. Settle it with a quick A/B test: measure time-to-task for keyboard users with both versions.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a skip link that only appears after the first tab press and hides until the next page load. This keeps the viewport clean for sighted mouse users while ensuring keyboard users get the bypass when they need it. The trade-off is a small delay in discoverability, but it’s worth it to avoid visual clutter.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users missing the skip link entirely if it only appears after the first tab press—many won’t realize it exists until they’ve already tabbed past it. A better alternative is a skip link that’s always present but visually hidden until focus arrives, then revealed only for keyboard users. Settle it with user testing: measure how often sighted keyboard users fail to find the skip link in both versions.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a **focus-triggered skip link**—high-contrast, full-width, visually hidden until focus arrives, then revealed—on every page. Must deliver: a working skip link that bypasses repetitive blocks for keyboard users without cluttering the viewport for others. Owner: Ramp.
